report.summary: The single change makes /opt/tempo/pi/tempo-profile.ts mode 0600. The COPY line has no --chown, so the file stays root:root. Every process in the image runs as `tempo` (uid 1000, `USER tempo`), so the file becomes unreadable to the Pi agent that has to load it with `-e /opt/tempo/pi/tempo-profile.ts`. Without the file, Pi fails to start, or starts without Tempo's tool_call guard and MCP server registration. That guard is what the spec says enforces tools.allow/deny and Pi read-only access. The image test that checks tempo can read the file (R_OK) would fail. The file holds no secrets: it is Tempo's own code and is also in the repository, so the tighter mode protects nothing. The image was not built in this run; the finding comes from reading the Dockerfile, the image test and the spec.

findings.text: tempo-profile.ts becomes root-owned mode 0600, so the `tempo` user that runs pi cannot read the extension. Pi then fails to load it, or runs without the tool_call allow/deny guard and MCP server registration the spec requires.

evidence.why: COPY without --chown makes the file root:root, and 0600 gives read access only to root. The image later sets `USER tempo` and starts tempod and its children, including pi-acp and pi, as uid 1000. The later `chmod 0755 /opt/tempo /opt/tempo/pi` changes only the directories, not the file. The pi wrapper passes `-e /opt/tempo/pi/tempo-profile.ts` (docs/01 Runtime and Agents.md, line 353), so loading the file fails with EACCES. packages/tempod/test/image.test.ts asserts `expect(() => accessSync("/opt/tempo/pi/tempo-profile.ts", constants.R_OK)).not.toThrow();` while running as uid 1000, so test:tempod:container would fail. The spec (docs/01, line 357) says this extension's tool_call guard is what enforces tools.allow/deny, and line 364 says it is used to deny write/edit for Pi read-only runs.

checked.risk: Build and runtime environment: the file's mode and owner, and which user reads it at runtime
Spec: how the Pi extension is installed and loaded, and its role in enforcing tool limits and read-only access
Security: whether 0600 protects anything (no secrets in the file; it is public repository code)
Tests: whether the image test checks that tempo can read the file (it does, with an R_OK assertion as uid 1000; gated on TEMPO_IMAGE_TEST=1, not run here)
Failure paths: a guard that fails closed versus a missing extension that leaves no enforcement

args.command: git log --oneline -1 && cat -n container/Dockerfile && grep -rn "tempo-profile" --include=* -I . 2>/dev/null | grep -v node_modules | head -30
